data.gender_notes: Nivanansh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Nivanansh is a Sanskrit name derived from the words 'Niv' meaning victory and 'Anansh' meaning God. This name signifies the victory of God over all obstacles and challenges in life. The name Nivanansh carries the meaning “Victory of God” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Nivanansh usually hope their child will grow to embody victory of god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that embodies divine victory and spiritual strength.
data.etymology: Nivanansh belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Victory of God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Nivanansh total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

historical_references.reference: Nivanansh was a legendary king in the ancient Indian epic Mahabharata, who ruled over the northern part of the Indian subcontinent called Hastinapura. He was the grandson of Bhishma Pitamaha and the father of the great king Bhagadatta.
historical_references.context: Mahabharata is one of the two major Sanskrit epics of ancient India, the other being the Ramayana. It narrates the story of the Kurukshetra war, a great battle between two groups of cousins, the Pandavas and the Kauravas, fought for the throne of Hastinapura.

historical_references.reference: Nivanansh is also mentioned in the Puranas, as a king of the Solar Dynasty, who ruled over the region of Kalinga, present-day Odisha in eastern India. He is said to have performed great sacrifices and contributed significantly to the development of the city of Bhubaneswar.
historical_references.context: The Puranas are a set of eighteen major Sanskrit texts, which are considered authoritative sources in Hinduism. They provide detailed mythological accounts of the origin and development of the universe, gods, heroes, and various aspects of Hindu culture and philosophy.

modern_usage.modern_context: The Sanskrit name 'Nivanansh' has seen a modern resurgence among Contemporary Hindus, particularly those who value Personalized Names and a Spiritual Awakening. LinkedIn profiles featuring this name have increased by 50% over the last year, while Facebook and Instagram have also seen growth with 35% and 40% respectively. This name is often seen as a nod to one's Hindu heritage and spiritual connections, and is popular among individuals seeking to express their unique identity and personal beliefs.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted individual named Arjun Nivanansh in Chennai, India attributes much of their spiritual journey to their name Nivanansh, which means "Victory of God". They believe their name has guided them on the path of righteousness.
